vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mystock
Version: 1.0.5

The MyStock skill bundle is a legitimate stock analysis tool providing a FastAPI backend and a Vue 3 frontend for tracking market data. It utilizes the `pywencai` library to query financial information from established sources like Tencent (qt.gtimg.cn) and East Money, and supports integration with various AI providers for investment insights. The installation and startup scripts (install.sh, start.sh) manage dependencies and local data storage in JSON files without any evidence of malicious behavior, data exfiltration, or unauthorized system modifications.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a stock assistant as described, but there are notable inconsistencies and privacy/credential risks (un-declared AI credentials, local portfolio data being sent to external AI providers, and global npm/pip operations) that you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Functionality (real-time quotes, limit-up analysis, shareholder monitoring, web UI) matches the code files. However the registry metadata declares no required environment variables while the code and docs clearly expect AI provider credentials (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY) and Node/jsdom for pywencai. The presence of large data files (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json, memos.json) included with the package is consistent with a self-hosted app but may be unexpected for a skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and backend code will incorporate local portfolio/watchlist/memos into the AI chat context and then call third-party AI endpoints (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, Minimax, Zhipu) if configured; that means local, potentially sensitive portfolio and notes are transmitted to external services. SKILL.md/start scripts also instruct global npm install -g jsdom and pip install -r requirements.txt, and the backend loads variables from .env (export $(cat .env | ...)), which can cause unexpected environment changes or inadvertently export secrets. The sync scripts will perform broad network queries (e.g., scanning HK codes) which may be heavy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote download/install spec in registry (no packaged installer), but SKILL.md and scripts instruct running local scripts (scripts/install.sh and start.sh) that will run npm -g jsdom and pip installs. Those operations pull packages from public registries (npm/pypi) — standard but you should review scripts/install.sh before running and avoid unnecessary global npm installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, yet backend/AI_CONFIG.md and ai_config.py expect AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and optional AI_BASE_URL/AI_MODEL). The code will send local portfolio/watchlist context to whatever AI provider you configure. Requiring an API key for an AI provider is reasonable for the chat feature, but the discrepancy between declared requirements and actual runtime expectations is misleading. Also the start script will export all entries from a .env file into the environment — review .env contents carefully.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not modify other skills. It reads and writes local data files (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json, memos.json) which is expected for a self-hosted app. This is normal but means data will be persisted locally and can be included in AI requests unless you change code/config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or running this skill:
- Inspect scripts/install.sh and backend/start.sh; do not run them blind. They will install global npm packages (jsdom) and Python dependencies.
- Review any .env provided; the service will export .env contents into the environment. Remove or redact any secrets you don't want exported.
- Be aware the backend builds an AI context that includes your portfolio/watchlist/memos and will send that to the configured AI provider (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, etc.). If you supply AI_API_KEY, your local portfolio and notes may be transmitted to third-party services—avoid providing keys if you don't want that.
- The package bundles portfolio_data.json and stock_codes.json with detailed entries and memos. Treat these as potentially sensitive sample data. If you are re-using this code, overwrite or remove those files before running to avoid leaking prior user's notes.
- Prefer running in an isolated environment (container or VM) and avoid global npm installs; consider installing jsdom locally or via nvm
- If you need only core read-only features (viewing local JSON), you can run with AI_PROVIDER=silence to avoid external API calls.
- If you want a higher-confidence assessment, provide the contents of scripts/install.sh and any un-truncated portions of backend/main.py (chat handler) so I can verify exactly what data is included in AI requests.
